source_text:
Μακάρια μὲν οὖν καὶ γενναῖα τὰ μαρτύρια πάντα τὰ κατὰ τὸ θέλημα τοῦ θεοῦ γεγονότα. δεῖ γὰρ εὐλαβεστέρους ἡμᾶς ὑπάρχοντας τῷ θεῷ τὴν κατὰ πάντων ἐξουσίαν ἀνατιθέναι.
τὸ γὰρ γενναῖον αὐτῶν καὶ ὑπομονητικὸν καὶ φιλοδέσποτον τίς οὐκ ἂν θαυμάσειεν; οἳ μάστιξιν: μὲν καταξανθέντες, ὥστε μέχρι τῶν ἔσω φλεβῶν καὶ ἀρτηριῶν τὴν τῆς σαρκὸς οἰκονομίαν θεωρεῖσθαι, ὑπέμειναν, ὡς καὶ τοὺς περιεστῶτας ἐλεεῖν καὶ ὀδύρεσθαι: τοὺς δὲ καὶ εἰς τοσοῦτον γενναιότητος ἐλθεῖν, ὥστε μήτε γρύξαι μήτε στενάξαι τινὰ αὐτῶν, ἐπιδεικνυμένους ἅπασιν ἡμῖν, ὅτι ἐκείνῃ τῇ ὥρᾳ βασανιζόμενοι τῆς σαρκὸς ἀπεδήμουν οἱ γενναιότατοι μάρτυρες τοῦ Χριστοῦ, μᾶλλον δέ, ὅτι παρεστὼς ὁ κύριος ὡμίλει αὐτοῖς.
καὶ προσέχοντες τῇ τοῦ Χριστοῦ χάριτι τῶν κοσμικῶν κατεφρόνουν βασάνων, διὰ μιᾶς ὥρας τὴν αἰώνιον ζωὴν ἐξαγοραζόμενοι. καὶ τὸ πῦρ ἦν αὐτοῖς ψυχρὸν τὸ τῶν ἀπηνῶν βασανιστῶν. πρὸ ὀφθαλμῶν γὰρ εἶχον φυγεῖν τὸ αἰώνιον καὶ μηδέποτε σβεννύμενον, καὶ τοῖς τῆς καρδίας ὀφθαλμοῖς ἀνέβλεπον τὰ τηρούμενα τοῖς ὑπομείνασιν ἀγαθά, ἃ οὔτε οὖς ἤκουσεν οὔτε ὀφθαλμὸς εἶδεν οὔτε ἐπὶ καρδίαν ἀνθρώπου ἀνέβη, ἐκείνοις δὲ ὑπεδείκνυτο ὑπὸ τοῦ κυρίου, οἵπερ μηκέτι ἄνθρωποι, ἀλλ’ ἤδη ἄγγελοι ἦσαν.
ὁμοίως δὲ καὶ οἱ εἰς τὰ θηρία κατακριθέντες ὑπέμειναν δεινὰς κολάσεις, κήρυκας ὑποστρωννύμενοι καὶ ἄλλαις ποικίλων βασάνων ἰδέαις κολαζόμενοι, ἵνα, εἰ δυνηθείη, ὁ τύραννος διὰ τῆς ἐπιμόνου κολάσεως εἰς ἄρνησιν αὐτοὺς τρέψῃ. πολλὰ γὰρ ἐμηχανᾶτο κατ’ αὐτῶν ὁ διάβολος.
thought_title: The martyrs' endurance and the tortures they suffered
orientation: The church of Smyrna is describing the courage of the recent martyrs, before the arrest of Polycarp.
pass_a_gloss: Blessed then and noble are all the martyrdoms that happened according to the will of God. For we must, being more reverent, attribute to God the authority over all things. For who would not marvel at their nobility and endurance and love for the Master? They, having been torn by scourges, so that the structure of the flesh was visible down to the inner veins and arteries, endured, so that even the bystanders pitied and lamented; and they reached such a degree of nobility that none of them either muttered or groaned, showing to us all that at that hour, while being tortured, the noblest martyrs of Christ were absent from the flesh, or rather, that the Lord stood by and was speaking with them. And attending to the grace of Christ, they despised the worldly tortures, purchasing eternal life through one hour. And the fire of the cruel torturers was cold to them. For they had before their eyes the escape from the eternal and never-quenched fire, and with the eyes of the heart they looked up at the good things kept for those who endured, which neither ear heard nor eye saw nor entered into the heart of a human, but were shown to them by the Lord, who were no longer humans but already angels. Likewise also those condemned to the wild beasts endured terrible punishments, being stretched on sharp shells and punished with other forms of varied tortures, so that, if he could, the tyrant might turn them to denial through the persistent punishment. For the devil contrived many things against them.

choices.why: The compound means love for the δεσπότης (Master/Lord), referring to Christ; rendering as 'love for the Master' preserves the personal relationship and the title.
οἰκονομία here means the arrangement or organization of the body's interior; 'structure' conveys the anatomical sense without modernizing.
κήρυξ can mean a herald, but in martyrdom contexts it refers to sharp shells or spikes used as instruments of torture; the context of being stretched on them supports this.
The verb means to be spread or laid under; in this torture context it means being stretched out upon the sharp shells.
The term refers to the persecuting authority, likely the proconsul or the devil's agent; 'tyrant' preserves the negative connotation.

bible_refs.note: ἃ οὔτε οὖς ἤκουσεν οὔτε ὀφθαλμὸς εἶδεν οὔτε ἐπὶ καρδίαν ἀνθρώπου ἀνέβη

pass_b_english: Blessed and noble, then, are all the martyrdoms that have taken place according to the will of God. For we must be reverent and assign to God authority over all things.

Who would not marvel at their nobility, their endurance, and their love for the Master? They were torn by scourges until the structure of the flesh could be seen down to the inner veins and arteries, yet they endured so steadfastly that even the bystanders wept and grieved. Some of them reached such heights of courage that not one of them cried out or groaned, showing all of us that in that hour of torture the noble martyrs of Christ were absent from the flesh—or rather, that the Lord stood by them and spoke with them.

Fixing their attention on the grace of Christ, they despised the torments of this world, purchasing eternal life at the cost of a single hour. The fire of their savage torturers felt cold to them, for they kept before their eyes the eternal life that is never quenched, and with the eyes of their hearts they gazed upon the good things reserved for those who endure—things no ear has heard, no eye has seen, and no human heart has conceived. But these were shown to them by the Lord, for they were no longer human beings but already angels.

In the same way, those condemned to the wild beasts endured terrible punishments: they were bound to stakes and tormented with other forms of varied tortures, so that the tyrant might, if possible, turn them to denial through relentless punishment. For the devil schemed many things against them.

problems.source_quote: ἃ οὔτε οὖς ἤκουσεν οὔτε ὀφθαλμὸς εἶδεν οὔτε ἐπὶ καρδίαν ἀνθρώπου ἀνέβη
problems.why: The source quotes Isaiah 64:4 (LXX) / 65:17, not 1 Corinthians 2:9. Paul cites this in 1 Cor, but the source text here quotes the OT directly.
problems.ruling: Greek phrase is an Isaiah LXX quote; translator adds (1 Cor 2:9) not present in source, mis‑attributing scripture.

problems.quote: they were stretched on sharp shells
problems.why: Greek says they were bound to stakes (or wooden posts), not stretched on shells.
problems.ruling: κήρυκας means heralds/messengers or stakes (from κήρυξ), not shells (κόγχη/ὄστρεον); 'stretched on sharp shells' is wrong.

edits.old: things no ear has heard, no eye has seen, and no human heart has conceived (1 Corinthians 2:9)
edits.new: things no ear has heard, no eye has seen, and no human heart has conceived (Isaiah 64:4)

edits.old: they were stretched on sharp shells

problems.source_quote: ἃ οὔτε οὖς ἤκουσεν οὐδὲ ὀφθαλμὸς εἶδεν οὐδὲ ἐπὶ καρδίαν ἀνθρώπου ἀνέβη
problems.why: The quoted verse is Isaiah 64:4 in the Septuagint, which corresponds to Isaiah 65:5 in modern numbering.

problems.quote: the eternal fire that is never quenched
problems.why: Greek refers to “the eternal” (life), not “eternal fire”; rendering as fire changes the metaphor.
problems.fix: the eternal life that is never quenched
problems.ruling: τὸ αἰώνιον alone means 'the eternal,' not 'eternal fire'; adding 'fire' imports concept from prior clause's πῦρ, distorting source.

problems.quote: kept before their eyes the eternal fire that is never quenched
problems.source_quote: πρὸ ὀφθαλμῶν ... ἔχον φυγεῖν τὸ αἰώνιον
problems.why: The Greek verb “φυγεῖν” (to flee) is omitted, losing the idea that they had before them the eternal to flee.
problems.fix: kept before their eyes the eternal life, which they could flee, that is never quenched
problems.ruling: φυγεῖν ('to flee') is omitted; Greek says they had 'the eternal' before their eyes to flee, not merely that they kept it before their eyes.

edits.old: the eternal fire that is never quenched
edits.new: the eternal life that is never quenched

edits.old: for they kept before their eyes the eternal fire that is never quenched
edits.new: for they kept before their eyes the eternal life, which they could flee, that is never quenched

fixed: The eternal fire issue was real: the source refers to the eternal life, not fire.
The omission of 'to flee' was real: the source includes φυγεῖν.
The scripture reference was real: LXX Isaiah 64:4 corresponds to modern Isaiah 65:5.

problems.source_quote: ἃ οὔτε οὖς ἤκουσεν οὔτε ὀφθαλμὸς εἶδεν οὔτε ἐπὶ καρδίαν ἀνθρώπου ἀνέβη
problems.why: The allusion is to Isaiah 64:4 (LXX 63:15) or 1 Cor 2:9, not Isaiah 65:5.
problems.ruling: Greek phrase matches 1 Cor 2:9 (or Isa 64:4 LXX), not Isaiah 65:5; citation is incorrect.

problems.why: The source does not contain a biblical citation; the English adds an unwarranted reference.
problems.ruling: Greek has no citation; English adds '(Isaiah 65:5)' but the quote matches 1 Cor 2:9/Isa 64:4 LXX, not Isa 65:5. Wrong reference added.

edits.old: things no ear has heard, no eye has seen, and no human heart has conceived (Isaiah 65:5).
edits.new: things no ear has heard, no eye has seen, and no human heart has conceived.

fixed: Removed the unwarranted biblical citation; the source has no citation here.
The allusion itself is preserved in the English wording without adding a reference.

problems.quote: the structure of the flesh could be seen down to the inner veins and arteries
problems.why: 'Structure' is odd for exposed anatomy; suggests 'framework' or 'very flesh' mistranslated.
problems.fix: Use 'inner structure' or 'musculature' if Greek allows.

problems.quote: the noble martyrs of Christ were absent from the flesh—or rather, that the Lord stood by them
problems.why: 'Absent from the flesh' contradicts 'Lord stood by them'; second clause seems correction.
problems.fix: Punctuate as editorial correction: 'absent from the flesh' [no], 'the Lord stood by them' [yes].

problems.quote: things no ear has heard, no eye has seen, and no human heart has conceived
problems.why: Alludes to Isaiah 64:4/1 Corinthians 2:9, but 'human heart' for 'mind' (νοῦς) misrepresents Pauline usage.
problems.fix: Note: quoting 1 Cor 2:9 which cites Isaiah; 'heart' here = inner person.

edits.old: the structure of the flesh could be seen down to the inner veins and arteries
edits.new: the inner structure of the flesh could be seen down to the veins and arteries

edits.old: the noble martyrs of Christ were absent from the flesh—or rather, that the Lord stood by them and spoke with them.
edits.new: the noble martyrs of Christ were absent from the flesh—or rather, the Lord stood by them and spoke with them.

edits.old: things no ear has heard, no eye has seen, and no human heart has conceived.
edits.new: things no ear has heard, no eye has seen, and no human mind has conceived.

fixed: The first problem is real: 'structure' is too vague for the exposed anatomy; changed to 'inner structure' to reflect the Greek 'τὴν τῆς σαρκὸς οἰκονομίαν' more precisely.
The second problem is real: the dash construction made the correction ambiguous; removed the dash after 'flesh' so the 'or rather' clause clearly corrects the first statement.
The third problem is real: 'heart' misrepresents the Pauline/Isaianic 'νοῦς' (mind); changed to 'mind' to align with 1 Corinthians 2:9.

problems.quote: things no ear has heard, no eye has seen, and no human mind has conceived
problems.why: This alludes to Isaiah 64:4 (or 1 Cor 2:9), but no citation is given and the wording differs from both.
problems.fix: Note the allusion to 1 Cor 2:9 / Isa 64:4.

edits.old: for they kept before their eyes the eternal life that is never quenched
edits.new: for they kept before their eyes escape from the eternal fire that is never quenched

edits.old: things no ear has heard, no eye has seen, and no human mind has conceived.
edits.new: things no ear has heard, no eye has seen, and no human heart has conceived (1 Corinthians 2:9).

fixed: The first problem about the eternal fire was real: the source says they had before their eyes escape from the eternal, never-quenched fire, not the fire itself as something to keep before their eyes. The English had been changed to 'eternal life' in a previous attempt, which was wrong. I restored the correct meaning with 'escape from the eternal fire that is never quenched'.

The second problem about the Scripture allusion was real: the source alludes to 1 Corinthians 2:9 (which itself quotes Isaiah 64:4), and the English lacked a citation. I added the citation and restored 'human heart' to match the source's 'καρδίαν ἀνθρώπου'.

problems.quote: no ear has heard, no eye has seen, and no human heart has conceived (1 Corinthians 2:9)
problems.why: The text reads 'no ear has heard, no eye has seen' but 1 Cor 2:9 reads 'eye has not seen, ear has not heard'; the order is reversed.
problems.fix: Correct to match 1 Cor 2:9 order or note the paraphrase.

edits.old: things no ear has heard, no eye has seen, and no human heart has conceived (1 Corinthians 2:9)
edits.new: things no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived (1 Corinthians 2:9)

fixed: The scripture citation order was reversed relative to 1 Corinthians 2:9; corrected to 'no eye has seen, no ear has heard'.

last_rejected.fix: the noblest martyrs of Christ were away from home from the flesh
last_rejected.ruling: ἀπεδήμουν = were away/absent from the flesh, fits context

last_rejected.quote: the eternal life that is never quenched
last_rejected.why: τὸ αἰώνιον here is 'the eternal fire/punishment', not 'eternal life'; context is what they flee.

last_rejected.ruling: τὸ αἰώνιον … σβεννύμενον = eternal (life) never extinguished

last_rejected.ruling: κήρυκας = stakes/poles; ὑποστρωννύμενοι = stretched under, translation acceptable
